world: Kestravane, Inc. is a fictional B2B SaaS company selling Kestravane Fleet, a fleet-operations platform (vehicle tracking, fuel and idle analytics, maintenance planning, cold-chain temperature monitoring) with optional hardware: TrakNode telematics units, TempSense temperature sensors and RoadLens cameras. It is sold per vehicle per month in three plans (Launch, Operations, Enterprise). The user is a Kestravane account executive talking to prospects and customers. The pack holds the current price list (v4.2, 1 July 2026), the superseded 2025 price list (v3.1), an unapproved draft 2027 price list, the current integration matrix, a security and compliance overview, the support and service level guide, the implementation guide and one customer story (Hollowmere Produce Logistics). Dorrowick Telematics and Pennoway Fleet are fictional competitors; nothing about their products or prices is documented.

files.title: Kestravane Fleet price list, version 4.2

facts.statement: The Launch plan costs $29 per vehicle per month on annual billing.
The Launch plan costs $35 per vehicle per month on monthly billing.
The Launch plan has a minimum fleet of 10 vehicles.
The Operations plan costs $47 per vehicle per month on annual billing.
The Operations plan costs $55 per vehicle per month on monthly billing.
The Operations plan has a minimum fleet of 25 vehicles.
The Enterprise plan costs $72 per vehicle per month on annual billing.
The Enterprise plan is sold on annual contracts only; monthly billing is not offered.
The Enterprise plan has a minimum fleet of 150 vehicles.
Trailers and other unpowered assets are billed at $11 per asset per month on any plan.
A fleet smaller than the plan minimum may subscribe to the plan but is billed for the minimum fleet size.
doc_needles: billed for the minimum fleet size

facts.statement: Vehicles added during a term are prorated to the end of the term at the contracted rate.
Annual billing is invoiced upfront on Net 30 terms.
The contracted rate is locked for the term, and renewal increases on annual contracts are capped at 6% per year.
The Driver Safety Scoring module costs $6 per vehicle per month.
The Fuel & Idle Analytics module costs $4 per vehicle per month.
The Maintenance Planner module costs $5 per vehicle per month.
The Cold Chain Monitoring module costs $3 per sensor per month and requires TempSense S2 sensors.
The Extended Video Retention module costs $8 per camera per month.
The NetSuite connector costs $400 per month and is available on Enterprise only.
A Technical Account Manager costs $18,000 per year and is available on Enterprise only.
Assisted data migration costs $1,500 one-time on Operations and is included in the Enterprise onboarding fee.
An on-site training day costs $1,400 per day plus travel.
A sandbox environment costs $150 per month on Operations and is included on Enterprise.
The Launch plan has no onboarding fee; setup is self-serve.
The Operations onboarding fee is $2,500, charged once.
The Enterprise onboarding fee is $7,500, charged once.
The onboarding fee covers the kickoff call, configuration, two remote admin training sessions and support through go-live; it does not cover hardware installation.
A TrakNode T4 telematics unit costs $89 per unit and one is required per vehicle.
A TempSense S2 temperature sensor costs $64 per sensor.
A RoadLens dual-facing camera costs $229 per camera.
Professional installation costs $45 per vehicle and covers every device fitted in the same visit.
Self-installation carries no charge.
Shipping is free on orders of 20 units or more in the contiguous United States; smaller orders ship for $75 flat.
All hardware carries a 3-year warranty with advance replacement.
Discounts apply to plan subscription fees only; modules, add-ons, hardware, installation and onboarding fees are never discounted.
The volume discount is applied automatically on annual billing; monthly billing is not eligible.
Fleets of 100 to 249 vehicles get a 5% volume discount.
Fleets of 250 to 499 vehicles get an 8% volume discount.
Fleets of 500 or more vehicles get a 12% volume discount.
Approval thresholds refer to the total discount off list, with the volume discount counted in.
An Account Executive may approve a total discount of up to 10% without further approval.
A total discount above 10% and up to 18% needs the Regional Sales Director's approval.
A total discount above 18% and up to 25% needs the VP Sales, after Deal Desk review.
A total discount above 25% is not available without a written exception from the CFO.
A quote that exceeds the signer's authority is not valid until the approval is recorded in the Deal Desk queue.
A three-year term locks the rate for the whole term but adds no further percentage discount.
A 21-day pilot of up to 5 vehicles with loaned hardware needs the Regional Sales Director's sign-off.
The price list says Enterprise fleets of 250 or more vehicles are assigned a named Customer Success Manager; smaller Enterprise fleets get the pooled team.
Monthly billing is charged to a card and can be cancelled with one full billing cycle of written notice.

must_not_infer: Nothing here says a price is negotiable outside the discount table, or that an Account Executive can exceed 10% total discount on their own.
The list does not say whether the Salesforce or HubSpot connectors carry a fee; it refers to the Integration Matrix for connector availability.
The list does not enumerate the features of each plan; a feature that is not named here is not thereby excluded from the product.
It gives no reason for the change in prices from the earlier list.
It says nothing about any competitor's prices.
The named Customer Success Manager threshold stated here (250 vehicles) disagrees with the Support Plans and Service Level Guide (300 vehicles); neither document settles it.

files.title: Kestravane Fleet integration matrix, edition 2026-Q3

facts.statement: The Salesforce connector is included at no additional charge on the Operations and Enterprise plans.
The Salesforce connector is two-way and syncs Accounts, Contacts, Cases and Work Orders on a 15-minute cycle.
Custom fields on the standard Salesforce objects can be mapped, up to 40 mapped fields per object.
Salesforce custom objects can be mapped on Enterprise only, up to 5 custom objects.
The Salesforce connector needs Salesforce Enterprise Edition or higher, or Professional Edition with API access enabled.
One Salesforce org can be connected per Kestravane account.
The HubSpot connector is available on Operations and Enterprise with no connector fee; it is one-way (Kestravane to HubSpot) and posts once an hour.
The HubSpot connector requires HubSpot Professional or higher.
The NetSuite connector is available on Enterprise only, as a $400 per month add-on.
The NetSuite connector exchanges five standard record types (Customer, Vendor, Item, Invoice, Purchase Order) as a nightly batch with on-demand sync.

NetSuite custom records, custom segments and other custom objects are not supported by the connector; customers build that part against the REST API; there is no committed date for custom record support.
doc_needles: are not supported by the connector

facts.statement: The Slack app is available on all plans at no fee, sends four kinds of alert, connects up to 25 channels and accepts no commands.
The Microsoft Teams app is in beta, available on Operations and Enterprise; beta features fall outside the uptime commitment.
QuickBooks Online is supported as a one-way invoice export on all plans.
WEX fuel card transactions are supported as an inbound data feed on Operations and Enterprise.
The REST API and webhooks are included on Operations and Enterprise at no fee and are not available on Launch.
The API rate limit on Operations is 600 requests per minute.
The API rate limit on Enterprise is 2,400 requests per minute.
There is no GraphQL endpoint and no bulk export endpoint; bulk extracts are delivered as scheduled CSV files.
No native connector exists for SAP S/4HANA, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks Desktop or Comdata fuel cards, and none is planned for 2026; they can be reached through the REST API.
None of the native connectors is available on the Launch plan.
Each connector connects to a single production instance; field mappings are changed by the customer's administrator.
Connector sync history is kept for 45 days.
An integration that does not appear in the matrix is not supported.
The matrix is edition 2026-Q3, effective 1 July 2026, published together with price list version 4.2.

must_not_infer: The matrix is not a roadmap: it gives no date for NetSuite custom record support or for a connector to SAP, Dynamics 365, Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Desktop.
It says nothing about what any competitor integrates with.
It does not cover product features such as electronic logging of driver hours.

files.title: Kestravane Fleet security and compliance overview, version 2026.2

facts.statement: The default hosting region is the United States (Oregon, with disaster recovery in Ohio), available on all plans.
An EU hosting region in Frankfurt, Germany is available on Enterprise only.
The region is chosen at provisioning; moving an account between regions after go-live is not supported.
No other hosting regions are available and there is no on-premises or customer-hosted deployment.
Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256.
Data in transit is protected with TLS 1.2 or higher.
Encryption keys are held in AWS Key Management Service and rotated every 12 months.
Customer-managed encryption keys are not offered.
doc_needles: Customer-managed encryption keys are not offered

facts.statement: Single sign-on (SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect) is included on Operations and Enterprise and not available on Launch.
SCIM 2.0 user provisioning is included on Enterprise only.
Single sign-on has been verified with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Ping Identity.
Audit logs are retained for 30 days on Launch, 90 days on Operations and 13 months on Enterprise.
Enterprise customers can pull audit events into their own SIEM through the audit log API.
Kestravane holds a SOC 2 Type II report covering 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, issued on 22 May 2026 by Harrowgate Assurance LLP.
The SOC 2 report covers the Security and Availability criteria; Confidentiality, Processing Integrity and Privacy are outside its scope.
Kestravane is not ISO 27001 certified: Stage 1 was completed in March 2026, Stage 2 is scheduled for November 2026, and certification is not expected before Q1 2027 with no date committed.
An external penetration assessment is carried out once a year; the most recent was completed in February 2026 by Corvane Labs; only a summary letter is shared.
Vehicle location and engine data is retained for 25 months and then deleted.
Temperature sensor readings are retained for 36 months.
Camera footage is retained for 45 days, or 180 days with Extended Video Retention.
After termination the customer can export data for 30 days; all customer data is deleted from production within 60 days of the termination date and from backups within a further 35 days.
Databases are backed up daily; the recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 8 hours.
A data processing addendum with the EU Standard Contractual Clauses is available on request for any plan.
Customers are notified 30 days before a new sub-processor is added.
Critical vulnerabilities are remediated within 7 days; security incidents affecting customer data are notified within 72 hours of confirmation.
Assurance reports are released under a non-disclosure agreement.
On Launch, multi-factor authentication is required for password logins.

must_not_infer: The overview does not mention HIPAA, business associate agreements or protected health information; Kestravane's position on them is unknown, neither compliant nor non-compliant.
It does not mention FedRAMP, PCI DSS or any other regime beyond those named.
Being in the middle of the ISO 27001 audit does not make Kestravane ISO 27001 certified.
The SOC 2 report does not cover the Confidentiality or Privacy criteria.
The overview states that it is not a complete list of controls, so silence on a topic is not a denial.

files.title: Kestravane Fleet support plans and service level guide, revision 3

facts.statement: Launch support is by email and help centre, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 18:00 Central, in English.
Operations support is by email and chat, 24 hours a day, Monday to Friday.
Enterprise support is by phone, email and chat, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Phone support is offered on Enterprise only; Operations customers are asked to open a chat or email ticket.
The Priority 1 first response target is 4 business hours on Launch, 1 hour on Operations and 30 minutes on Enterprise.
The Priority 2 first response target is 1 business day on Launch, 4 business hours on Operations and 2 hours on Enterprise.
The Priority 3 first response target is 3 business days on Launch, 1 business day on Operations and 8 business hours on Enterprise.
Response targets are for a first response within the plan's support hours; they are not resolution times and carry no service credit.
The Launch plan has no uptime commitment.
The Operations plan has a monthly uptime commitment of 99.5%.
On Operations the service credit is 5% of the monthly subscription fee if uptime is below 99.5%, and 10% if it is below 99.0%.
The Enterprise plan has a monthly uptime commitment of 99.95%.
On Enterprise the service credit is 10% of the monthly subscription fee if uptime is below 99.95%, and 25% if it is below 99.0%.

For annual contracts the monthly subscription fee is one-twelfth of the annual plan fee; a credit must be claimed in writing within 45 days of the end of the month and is applied to the next invoice, not paid in cash.
doc_needles: one-twelfth of the annual plan fee

facts.statement: Service credits are the sole remedy for missed uptime.
Scheduled maintenance is on Sundays between 02:00 and 05:00 Central, announced 5 business days ahead, limited to 6 hours a month, and excluded from uptime.
Beta features, the customer's own network and third-party systems on the other end of a connector are outside the uptime commitment.

The stated uptime figures are the only ones offered; a different uptime figure, credit schedule or response-time commitment is a non-standard term needing written approval from the VP Customer Operations and Legal through Deal Desk; account teams must not offer or imply other service levels.
The support guide says Enterprise accounts with 300 or more vehicles get a named Customer Success Manager with a quarterly business review.
Enterprise accounts with fewer than 300 vehicles are served by the pooled Customer Success team with a business review twice a year.
Operations accounts are served by the pooled Customer Success team with a group check-in webinar each quarter.
A Technical Account Manager can be added to any Enterprise account as a paid add-on.
A Priority 1 ticket unresolved after 2 hours is escalated to the Duty Incident Manager; at 4 hours the VP Customer Operations is notified.
During a Priority 1 incident Enterprise customers get an update every hour and Operations customers every 4 hours.
Any customer can request an escalation at any time; Enterprise customers can call the escalation line.
Hardware that fails under warranty is replaced in advance; the replacement ships within 2 business days of the fault being confirmed.
Support languages are English on Launch, English and Spanish on Operations, and English, Spanish and French on Enterprise.
Support does not cover the customer's own API code, editing connector mappings, or on-site visits.
The guide is revision 3, effective 1 July 2026.

must_not_infer: A 99.95% commitment in the guide does not authorise a seller to put 99.99% or any other figure in a contract.
Response targets are not resolution guarantees.
The named Customer Success Manager threshold stated here (300 vehicles) disagrees with the current price list (250 vehicles); neither document settles it.
Nothing here says a non-standard term will be approved if requested.

files.title: Kestravane Fleet implementation and onboarding guide, version 2.3

facts.statement: A rollout has six stages; Launch is self-run, Operations is guided by an onboarding specialist, Enterprise is run by a named project manager with a weekly status call.
The kickoff call is normally held within 5 business days of contract signature, and every duration is counted from the kickoff call, not the signature.
A Launch rollout typically takes 5 to 10 business days.
An Operations rollout of up to 200 vehicles typically takes 30 days from kickoff to go-live.
An Operations rollout of more than 200 vehicles takes 45 to 75 days.
An Enterprise rollout takes 60 to 90 days.

The durations are planning estimates, not commitments; go-live dates are not written into order forms; a committed date exists only in a Statement of Work signed by the Director of Professional Services after a scoping call; account teams cannot commit to a date on their own.
The most common causes of delay are vehicles not released for installation, a late vehicle list, and waiting for single sign-on configuration.
Hardware arrives 7 to 10 business days after the hardware order is placed.
Professional installation is booked at least 10 business days ahead; one two-person crew fits about 15 vehicles per working day at a single depot.
A professional installation keeps a vehicle off the road for about 40 minutes; a self-installed TrakNode on a light vehicle takes about 20 minutes; heavy trucks need the 9-pin harness.
Each native connector takes 3 to 5 business days to configure and validate, and the customer's administrator for the connected system must be available.
Single sign-on setup needs the customer's identity provider team; allow one week.
The customer names a project lead, with authority over vehicle scheduling, within 3 business days of the kickoff call.
The customer supplies the vehicle list (VIN, licence plate, home depot, vehicle class) at least 5 business days before the first installation date.
The customer releases vehicles on the agreed days, supplies the driver roster, sends administrators to two 90-minute remote training sessions and signs the go-live checklist.
Only the most recent 24 months of trip and location history can be migrated; older trip history is not loaded under any plan.
Maintenance history can be migrated for up to 5 years.
Driver safety scores and camera footage cannot be migrated.
Migration files must be UTF-8 CSV in the Kestravane templates; ready-made converters exist for exports from Dorrowick Telematics and Pennoway Fleet.
Assisted data migration is a paid service on Operations and part of the onboarding fee on Enterprise; Launch customers load their own files.
doc_needles: is a paid service on Operations

facts.statement: Tracking hardware from another supplier cannot be reused; every vehicle needs a TrakNode unit.
A rollout is live when 95% of contracted vehicles have reported data for three consecutive days, training is complete and the checklist is signed.
For 14 days after go-live the onboarding specialist or project manager stays assigned (hypercare); after that the account moves to standard support.
Changes after kickoff are handled through a change note and can move the go-live date.
Two remote administrator training sessions are included on Operations and Enterprise; on-site training is a paid day.
A signed Statement of Work takes precedence over the guide.

must_not_infer: A typical duration of 30 days is an estimate, not a guarantee; the seller has no authority to promise a go-live date.
The guide does not say an exception will be made for trip history older than 24 months.
The guide gives no fee amounts; those are in the price list.
Having a converter for Dorrowick exports says nothing about Dorrowick's product, quality or prices.

files.title: Customer story: Hollowmere Produce Logistics

facts.statement: Hollowmere Produce Logistics is a family-owned refrigerated carrier based in Yakima, Washington.
Hollowmere's fleet is 212 refrigerated trucks at three depots, with about 260 drivers.
Hollowmere runs the Operations plan with the Fuel & Idle Analytics and Cold Chain Monitoring modules.
Each Hollowmere truck carries one TrakNode and two TempSense sensors, 424 sensors in all.
Hollowmere did not take cameras or Driver Safety Scoring and uses none of the native connectors.
The measured period was 1 March to 31 August 2025, compared with the same six months of 2024.
Average engine idling per truck per day fell from 73 minutes to 59 minutes, 19% lower.
Fuel consumed per 100 miles fell from 16.4 to 15.4 gallons, 6.1% lower.
Temperature-related load claims fell from 41 to 17.
Claims accepted without dispute fell from 33 to 6.
Hollowmere estimates the lower fuel consumption was worth about $186,000 over the six months.
Hollowmere's finance team puts payback on hardware and first-year subscription at under 9 months.
The figures come from Hollowmere's own records and have not been audited by Kestravane or a third party.
There was no control group; the comparison is the same fleet against its previous year.
Hollowmere launched a driver coaching programme in April 2025, during the measured period; its effect cannot be separated from Kestravane's.
The results are from one refrigerated fleet in one region and are not a forecast or a promise of results.
Hollowmere's own maintenance staff fitted the hardware, depot by depot.
The customer story was published in February 2026.
The Hollowmere spokesperson is Wendeline Aukes, Director of Fleet Operations.
Hollowmere is evaluating Maintenance Planner and has asked for trailer door sensors, which Kestravane does not currently make.

must_not_infer: The Hollowmere results are not a promise or forecast for any other customer.
The improvement cannot be attributed to Kestravane alone, because a driver coaching programme ran in the same period.
The story gives no rollout duration and says nothing about how long go-live took.
No other customer's results are documented.
